findings.found: 004-16 (2019): "Gradually build how long you stay in a cold shower", with no upper limit. 540-63 (2023) is nested under it with no `later`: "No need to push cold exposure significantly beyond the sweet spot of about 11 minutes per week or set records" (540-62 gives about a minute and a half per day). Someone who reads only 004-16 keeps lengthening the shower; the host's later claim says to stop at about a minute and a half a day. That changes what a person does, so it is a Later view, not a hedge. As rendered, 540-63 also sits in 'How to practice' and names "the sweet spot", which is defined only in 540-62 in 'How much'.
findings.fix: In 'How to practice', change the nested line under 004-16 to `later 540-63` (newer after older, 004-16 kept). Leave the 540-62 group in 'How much' as it is.

findings.found: The 289-34 group repeats the brown-fat groups of 140 and 090 as a separate top-level line in the same section. 289-36 "The cold engine, brown fat, helps keep you warm and adapt to cold" is the claim of 140-35 "Brown fat is basically our body's warmth engine: the more we have, the more easily we stay warm" (with 090-53). 289-35 "Every little bit of cold trains the cold engine, brown fat: a 30-second or 10-minute cold shower..." is the claim of 140-36 "Every time you expose yourself to cold, your body responds by building brown fat" and 090-49, with another scope (even a little cold, vs 'any decent period'). 289-34 (brown fat trained like muscles with push-ups) is the muscle image of 090-51 and 140-37. These are different strengths or scopes of the same claims, so a missed group, not a merge.
findings.fix: In 'Adapting to cold', nest the whole 289-34 line (with 289-35 and 289-36) under 140-35, so the 'warmth engine' claim is one group. Optionally move the 140-36 group (now in 'Physical effects') into 'Adapting to cold' beside it and nest 289-35 under 140-36 instead.

findings.found: Two top-level groups in 'Willpower, discipline and resistance' make the same claim: a cold shower builds the ability or willingness to choose a discomfort because of where it leads. 004-24 group: 174-79 "builds willpower: you choose your path intentionally even though it's uncomfortable in the moment, because you know it leads to a good place", 289-28 and 289-30 "stepping into a little discomfort because it leads where I want to go". 240-19 group: 240-19 "Probably the biggest benefit of cold showers: they strengthen your ability to just do an uncomfortable thing", 350-10 "Maybe among the most important benefits... they strengthen your willingness to make a choice that is uncomfortable in the moment but benefits you in the long run". The strengths differ ("the biggest benefit" vs "probably" vs "maybe among the most important" vs plain), so a group, not a merge. Also 240-21 "Every cold shower strengthens your ability and willingness to say 'this thing that I'm about to do is gonna be uncomfortable, but I'm gonna do it anyway'" sits in the 114-33 group although it is the plain version of 240-19 from the same episode, and 092-43 "A daily cold shower also builds your willingness to get uncomfortable, to face resistance head on" sits in the resistance group with the same claim.
findings.fix: Nest the 240-19 line (with 350-10 and 350-12) under 004-24. Move 240-21 and 092-43 from their present groups to nested lines under 240-19. Leave 114-33 as its own group (choosing the uncomfortable thing at the start of the day).

findings.found: Same registry split in episode 140.
